I couldn't do this research, so I have no notes for you. My one attempt to fetch the sources failed: the research tool told me I had no calls left before it returned any pages or search results. That means I haven't read anything from enduringword.com, biblehub.com, studylight.org, preceptaustin.org, gotquestions.org, netbible.org or any of the other approved sites.

You asked me to report only what the pages actually say, with a URL for every point. Without any pages, writing the notes would mean filling them from my own memory, so I've written none.

**What I would have read**, in case you want to run it again or check them yourself:
- **Verse-by-verse commentaries:**
  - enduringword.com/bible-commentary/ezekiel-28/
  - biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/ezekiel/28.htm
  - biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/ezekiel/28.htm
  - biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/ezekiel/28.htm
  - preceptaustin.org's Ezekiel 28 commentary
- **Vv. 12–19:** gotquestions.org's article on whether Ezekiel 28 describes Satan. This is the passage where traditions differ most: is it the human king of Tyre, Satan, or both?
- **Modern scholarship:** the netbible.org translator's notes on Ezekiel 28, and any bibleodyssey.org articles on Tyre, Eden or the cherub.
- **Catholic and Orthodox:** searches of catholic.com, newadvent.org and oca.org on Ezekiel 28 and Lucifer.
- **Protestant traditions:** searches for Reformed, Baptist, Wesleyan, Pentecostal and Lutheran teachers on the passage, such as Calvin or Spurgeon via ccel.org or spurgeon.org.

If you ask again in a new message, I'll retry these fetches and searches and write the notes verse by verse, with a URL for each point.
